key_insight: A multi-step screening workflow using automated EHR flags followed by structured staff review greatly narrows a large sepsis candidate pool into a smaller, higher-yield enrollment set.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help research teams efficiently recruit better-characterized sepsis cohorts for biomarker and host-response studies without overwhelming clinical staff.
method: Automated EHR screening identified adults with suspected sepsis using SIRS criteria, recent culture/PCR, and new antibiotic exposure.
Non-physician study staff performed structured chart review as an enrichment step before discussion with the primary clinical team.
Enrolled patients were physician-adjudicated into diagnostic categories and compared with a composite sepsis-likely definition.
evidence_signal: In 4,318 screened patients, 1,220 were flagged and 288 enrolled; among enrolled patients, 73% were adjudicated as sepsis, and the 9-week evaluation included 907 screened encounters.
watch_item: Because the workflow depends on local EHR rules, staffing, and team discussions, performance and feasibility may vary across hospitals and patient populations.
paper_title: Efficiency of a Multi-step Screening and Enrichment Process for Prospective Sepsis Cohort Enrollment
